sentence: This project studies how a transcription factor in tumors changes collagen and how that affects immune cells in cancers that resist immune therapy.
This project studies how bacteria and fungi in the human gut interact and how those interactions affect immunity.
This project builds machine learning tools that improve patient safety, monitoring and communication during pediatric transports between facilities.
This project builds a complete map of the brain and body connections of the larval zebrafish to study how the brain and heart interact.
This project studies how mechanosensitive channels in bacteria open and close.
This project teaches physicians about cancer genomics so they can use genomic test results in the care of patients.
This project studies how neurons in the fruit fly visual system pick out features from what the fly sees.
This project uses a digital health software platform to find people who may benefit from genetic testing for hereditary cancer, using family medical history.
This project uses artificial intelligence and directed evolution to create biosensors that detect many kinds of terpenes.
This project offers imaging tools to study tumor growth, progression, metastasis and therapeutic responses in cancer cells and tissues.
This project designs hardware and beamformer strategies to build a low cost, real time ultrasound imaging system for volumetric imaging.
This project studies how family functioning affects obesity risk behaviors in Hispanic adolescents, using ecological momentary assessment.
This project uses a mouse model and DNA sequencing to study how genetic and epigenetic factors make DNA repeats unstable in myotonic dystrophy.
This project combines biomedical investigation with the art of clinical medicine in an integrated course of study.
This project tries to fix factual mistakes and unfaithful reasoning in Large Language Models used in biomedicine and healthcare.
This project studies how connections between epigenetic marks decide how sensitive different genomic loci are to arsenic exposure.
This project provides core services and resources to support vision research on blinding eye diseases such as glaucoma, macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy.
This project looks for DNAzymes that modify the amino groups of cytosine, guanine and adenine at chosen sites in DNA and RNA.
This project uses bioinformatics to study cell-specific and metabolic changes in heart tissue and blood samples from patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
This project develops label-free imaging that examines cells and tissues in living skin, including collagen fibers, using computation and deep-learning.
